basics.name: Kendall A. Reid
basics.label: Ph.D. Student in Computer Science, Johns Hopkins University
basics.summary: I am interested in creating AI systems for scientific research in human genetics and genomics. Current models excel on well-defined problems but struggle when evidence is uncertain or contradictory. I aim to build systems that overcome these limitations, and to develop rigorous evaluations to ensure that their reasoning is transparent and conclusions can be trusted. By harnessing these models for human genetics, we can discover the mechanisms of disease and identify therapeutic targets.

work.name: Johns Hopkins University, Biostatistics, and Neuroscience
highlights: Designed and led a study of whether latent variable models isolate known gene programs in single-cell data. First author; manuscript in preparation.

Led the computational biology for a companion study applying latent variable models to amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) to identify similarities and differences in disease pathology. Second author; manuscript in preparation.

work.name: Johns Hopkins University, Department of Epidemiology
highlights: Developed an agent-based simulation library for HIV population dynamics using Dask.
Co-authored a study that used this library to forecast the effect of a BMI maintenance intervention on diabetes risk.

Led the interpretability analysis for a study of virologic failure in people with HIV, investigating whether a linear Cox model and a nonlinear deep survival network identified the same influential risk factors. Third author; manuscript in preparation.

work.name: Johns Hopkins University
highlights: Recruited a team of researchers from across the globe to investigate the discordance in metrics used to evaluate perturbation prediction models, resulting in a preprint. Second author; submission in progress.
Designed a controlled comparison of Wasserstein critics and discriminators for batch correction in single-cell data. First author; manuscript in preparation.

Showed that computing energies along a protein diffusion model's reverse diffusion trajectory with trapezoidal integration is a discrete realization of the Stratonovich integral, contributing to a publication on protein energies in diffusion models.
Built a blended genome-exome polygenic risk score for ketamine response in treatment-resistant depression, in collaboration with the Broad Institute. First author; under review.
